{{Short description|American mathematician}}
'''James Thomas (J. Thomas "Tom") Beale''' (born 1947) is an American mathematician, specializing in [[fluid dynamics]], [[partial differential equation]]s, and [[numerical analysis]].<ref name=FAN2010>{{cite web|title=Fluid dynamics, Analysis, and Numerics 2010: A conference in honor of J. Thomas Beale|date=June 2020|website=Department of Mathematica, Duke University|url=https://services.math.duke.edu/conferences/FAN2010/beale.html}}</ref>

J. Thomas Beale grew up in [[Savannah, Georgia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Lillian Neidlinger Beale|newspaper=Savannah Morning News|date=October 8, 2004|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/savannah/name/lillian-beale-obituary?pid=2686812}}</ref> In 1967 he graduated from [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech) with a B.S. in mathematics.<ref>{{cite book|title=Seventy-Third Annual Commencement|date=June 9, 1967|publisher=California Institute of Technology|url=https://campuspubs.library.caltech.edu/2528/1/June_9,_1967.pdf}}</ref> In 1973 he received his PhD in mathematics from Stanford University. His PhD thesis ''Purely imaginary scattering frequencies for exterior domains''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=u8VGAAAAIAAJ|title = Purely Imaginary Scattering Frequencies for Exterior Domains|last1 = Beale|first1 = James Thomas|year = 1973}}</ref> was written under the supervision of [[Ralph S. Phillips]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=40266}}</ref> Soon after receiving his PhD Beale became a faculty member at [[Tulane University]]. In 1983 he resigned from Tulane University and became a professor at [[Duke University]], where he retired as professor emeritus in 2016.<ref name=retirement>{{cite web|title=Professor J. Thomas Beale Retires|website=Department of Mathematics, Duke University|date=May 20, 2016|url=https://math.duke.edu/news/professor-j-thomas-beale-retires}}</ref>

In 1994 Beale was an invited speaker with talk ''Analytical and numerical aspects of fluid interfaces'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich.<ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-9078-6_98|chapter=Analytical and Numerical Aspects of Fluid Interfaces|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1994, Zürich|year=1995|last1=Beale|first1=J. Thomas|publisher=Birkhäuser|location=Basel|pages=1055–1064|isbn=978-3-0348-9897-3}}</ref>

From June 28 to 30, 2010, the mathematics department of Duke University held a conference in his honor.<ref name=FAN2010/>
